key_insight: A decision model that acts poorly can still teach effectively by judging actions after their consequences are visible.
engineering_relevance: Retrospective action-level feedback can improve reinforcement learning for long-horizon agents without requiring the teacher to be a strong actor.
method: Compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and trajectory-aware judges on ALFWorld.
Evaluate whether asking if each action helped distinguishes useful from useless actions.
Use JEV as a teacher for a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy on ALFWorld and WebShop.
evidence_signal: JEV teaching improved success over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop.
watch_item: Judging relies on completed trajectories, and teacher gains are demonstrated for one teacher–policy pairing on two benchmarks.
paper_title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
